Theme

Money, work & business · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

owe verb

also owing, owed, owe money, how much do I owe you?

classical

Mart. 2.3.1: Sexte, nihil dēbēs
Vulg. Lc. 16.5: quantum dēbēs dominō meō?

dēbeō, dēbēre, dēbuī, dēbitum

verb, second conjugation

owe (money, thanks)

What is owed in the accusative, the creditor in the dative: pecūniam alicui dēbēre; a debt is dēbitum or aes aliēnum (see debt). With an infinitive dēbeō is ought, of duty (see be supposed to).

Examples

  • Sexte, nihil dēbēs, nīl dēbēs, Sexte, fatēmur: dēbet enim, sī quis solvere, Sexte, potest.

    You owe nothing, Sextus, nothing at all, Sextus, we admit it: for only a man who can pay owes anything, Sextus.Mart. 2.3

  • quantum dēbēs dominō meō? at ille dīxit: centum cadōs oleī.

    How much do you owe my master? And he said: A hundred jars of oil.Vulg. Lc. 16.5–6

  • Aesōpī nōmen sīcubi interposuerō, cui reddidī jam prīdem quicquid dēbuī, auctōritātis esse scītō grātiā

    If I bring in Aesop’s name anywhere, though I paid him long ago all I owed him, know that it is for the sake of his authorityPhaedr. 5 prol. 1–3

See also debt, pay, bill, loan, borrow, be supposed to.
